ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two terminals, upper and lower, on the left side, beside which the positive and negative terminals of the AC voltage u are marked; the upper branch is a capacitor labeled C, and the wire on the right connects downward to the bottom branch; the bottom branch has a resistor labeled R. Therefore, capacitor C and resistor R are connected in series across the two ends of voltage source u. Reasoning calculation: From u = 100√2 sin(1000t) V, it can be known that the RMS value of the voltage U = 100 V, and the angular frequency ω = 1000 rad/s. The capacitance C = 25 μF, so the magnitude of the capacitive reactance X_C = 1/(ωC) = 1/(1000 × 25 × 10^-6) = 40 Ω. The magnitude of the impedance of the series RC circuit |Z| = √(R^2 + X_C^2) = √(30^2 + 40^2) = 50 Ω. The RMS value of the current I = U/|Z| = 100/50 = 2 A. The circuit has no inductive element, and reactive power comes only from the capacitor, whose magnitude Q = I^2 X_C = 2^2 × 40 = 160 var; if the signed convention is adopted, capacitive reactive power is -160 var.
